Wayne Local school dates per The Spartan (September and October 2026) and the district Community Events & Activities newsletter (October 2026) and Board Meeting Recap (October and November 2026). Waynesville Elementary book fair, PTO meeting and Holiday Shop dates per the school’s upcoming-events graphic (November 2026). Mary L. Cook Public Library programs per the library's monthly newsletter (November 2026). Recurring items (rodeo, commissioners, ghost walk, Lions Club meetings on the 2nd and 4th Tuesdays) show the next occurrence. Warren County Park District events page SUSPENDED as a source per Cap'n (2026-10-03): it sits behind a Cloudflare bot challenge (403 since 2026-09-24). Do not fetch it or report it as failing; its items from the 2026-09-23 check are kept until they expire. Resume only when Cap'n provides a working source. Event notes and dateLabels are shown to readers: write them for readers (what, when, where, and a helpful pointer like "check the event website for times" when a detail is missing). Never put editorial or process notes in them ("not published", "confirm before printing", "corrected from", "checked on"); record corrections in the commit message instead. Tag Christmas-season community events (tree lightings, Santa visits, holiday markets, single-date light shows) with "holiday" so they also appear on the Holiday Lights guide. Waynesville area vs. regional: an event counts as Waynesville-area when its venue names Waynesville, Corwin, Harveysburg, Oregonia, Ridgeville, Lytle, Mount Holly, Crosswick, Caesar Creek or ZIP 45068/45054/45065 (see src/lib/events.js); always put the town in the venue. Optional "cost" (e.g. "Free", "$5 adults, kids free") and "accessibility" (e.g. "Wheelchair accessible; parking behind the building") show as a line under the event, only when the organizer or its source says so. Set "local": true or false to override (e.g. an online survey about Waynesville, or an out-of-town group serving Waynesville families). Optional "orgs": ["<exact name from churches.json>"] ties an event to a church on the Churches page when its venue doesn't name the church.

items.title: Kings Island
items.dateLabel: Bonus Weekend Nov 7–8; WinterFest select nights Nov 27–Dec 31
items.note: Park hours: Nov 7–8 Bonus Weekend 11 AM–7 PM. WinterFest opens Nov 27 (Nov 27 & 29 5–10 PM, Nov 28 4–10 PM) and runs select nights through Dec 31. Waterpark closed. Check the park calendar for any changes.

items.title: WinterFest at Kings Island
items.note: Per Kings Island: holiday event on select nights. Opening weekend hours Nov 27 & 29 5–10 PM, Nov 28 4–10 PM. December open dates on the park calendar: Dec 4–6, 11–23 and 26–31; check the calendar for each night's hours.
items.cost: Free for ages 65+ (born on or before Dec. 31, 1961) with Kings Island’s free 2026 Senior Admission: register on the park’s ticket site, limit two per order, ID required at the gate, parking not included. Others need a ticket or season pass.

items.venue: Mary L. Cook Public Library, 381 Old Stage Rd, Waynesville
items.note: Bid in person on holiday gift baskets, decorations and other items donated by area businesses and neighbors. Bidding opens Friday, Nov 20 at noon and closes Thursday, Dec 10 at 7:00 PM. Proceeds from the Friends of the Mary L. Cook Library support the library’s free programs for all ages and its new Playscape.

items.note: Drop letters to Santa in the library's special mailbox. Letters mailed by Dec 15 get a reply from Santa's elves, who try to answer before Dec 25.

items.title: Santa Holiday Open House at the Library
items.venue: Mary L. Cook Public Library, 381 Old Stage Rd, Waynesville
items.note: Photos with Santa, letter writing, a holiday craft, the library's new Elf Academy, and refreshments from the Friends of the Library. Registration required, beginning Monday, Nov 9: call the library at 513-897-4826 or sign up at the front desk.

items.title: North Warren County Transportation Plan — online survey closes
items.note: Last day to comment online on the plan, including options for a new I-75 to I-71 connection (one would follow US 42 and S.R. 73 through Waynesville and Corwin) and priority intersections such as S.R. 73 and US 42 in Waynesville. The survey opened Oct. 28.

items.title: Town Square Days: Step into Stars Hollow
items.dateLabel: Sat, Nov 21 · 10 AM–7 PM; Sun, Nov 22 · 10 AM–5 PM
items.note: "A Day in Waynesville": downtown Waynesville steps into Stars Hollow for the weekend, 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. Saturday and 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday, rain or shine. Presented by the Waynesville Merchant Association and sponsored by Taylor's Coffee & Creamery. For the event shuttle, park at the Waynesville Performing Arts Center, 659 Dayton Rd.; the shuttle stop downtown is at Main and North streets by LCNB, and there is more parking around town. All ticketed cast member interactions are at the Performing Arts Center. Main Street is closed between North and Miami streets, where the food trucks line up, and part of High Street west of Main is closed too. Restrooms are at 86 S. Main St. and behind the Main Street event tent. DORA drinks are available at Stone House Tavern, Bentino's Pizza and Village Restaurant. Free photo spots: Hailstorm Vintage, Collected & Co., Lucky Kat and Taylor's Coffee on Main; Blitzen & Pine on Miami; and the gazebo and town sign behind Taylor's Coffee, Buckeye Charm, Green Feather Apothecary and Art Expressions on High. Twenty-one shops are event partners. Tap the title for the event map.

items.title: Waynesville Christmas Rewind
items.note: A nostalgic Christmas evening downtown: shop local for last-minute gifts, hot cocoa, Christmas music and classic-Christmas-movie fun. Free, no tickets needed.

items.title: Free Thanksgiving food baskets for Waynesville families
items.note: MorningStar Baptist Church is offering Thanksgiving food baskets to Waynesville families who could use a little extra help this year. To ask for one for yourself or someone you know, text 937-270-2330, email Outreach@morningstardayton.org or message the church on Facebook.

items.note: The Waynesville Area Chamber of Commerce holiday networking mixer. Check the Chamber events page for details.

items.title: Town Square Days Dance Marathon
items.venue: Turn Out Dance Academy, 274 S. Main St., Waynesville
items.note: A public dance marathon with a 1940s theme (plus some 2000s music) during Town Square Days. No dance experience needed; prizes for one couple and one single winner. Entry is two canned goods or a $5 donation for the Waynesville Food Pantry. Arrive by 11:15 AM; no shoes in the studio, and a short waiver is required.

items.title: Waynesville Lions Club Pancake Breakfast & Craft Bazaar
items.dateLabel: Sat, Dec 5 · Breakfast & Santa 8–11 AM, bazaar 8 AM–3 PM
items.venue: Waynesville Elementary School, 659 Dayton Rd, Waynesville
items.note: The Lions Club’s annual breakfast and bazaar. Pancake breakfast 8–11 AM ($8 adults, $5 children) and visits with Santa 8–11 AM; craft bazaar with 30 vendors 8 AM–3 PM, free admission. New this year: a free children’s crafting table, live performances by local children, and a free raffle for a basket worth over $300 (visit all 30 vendor booths to fill your card). All proceeds benefit the Waynesville Food Pantry.

items.title: Lebanon Horse-Drawn Carriage Parade & Christmas Festival
items.dateLabel: Sat, Dec 5 · festival 10 AM–8 PM; parades 1 PM and 7 PM
items.note: Ohio’s largest horse-drawn carriage parade returns to downtown Lebanon, with two parades (1:00 and 7:00 p.m., the evening one by candlelight) and a Christmas festival and market from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m., per the Lebanon Area Chamber of Commerce.

items.title: Playoff football, Region 20 final: Waynesville vs. Bishop Fenwick
items.venue: Lakota East High School, 6840 Lakota Ln., Liberty Township (neutral site)
items.note: Division V, Region 20 final at a neutral site, Lakota East High School in Liberty Township, 7 p.m., with Waynesville as the home team. Waynesville beat Graham 14-7 in the semifinal; Bishop Fenwick, from Franklin, won 27-13 at Williamsburg. Check the Spartans' pages for ticket details; tap Details for the team's graphic.

items.title: Wayne Local Schools Board of Education — Regular Meeting
items.venue: WLS Performing Arts Center (second floor), 625 Dayton Rd, Waynesville
items.note: Per Wayne Local Board Meeting Recap (Nov 2026): regularly scheduled business meeting. Open to the public.

items.title: Spartan Holiday Food Drive
items.note: Per Wayne Local Schools Community Events & Activities newsletter (Oct 2026): the Waynesville Student Council and American Legion Holiday Food Drive collects nonperishable food for local families through American Legion Post 615. Students drop off items in homerooms (WES) or second-period classes (WMS/WHS).

items.title: WMS/WHS Winter Art Exhibition
items.venue: WLS Performing Arts Center, 625 Dayton Rd, Waynesville
items.note: Per Wayne Local Schools Community Events & Activities newsletter (Oct 2026): annual one-night show of artwork by students in grades 6–12.

items.title: Warren County Career Pathway Expo
items.venue: Warren County Fairgrounds Event Center, Lebanon
items.note: Per Wayne Local Schools Community Events & Activities newsletter (Oct 2026): local professionals are invited to support students from Waynesville High School and other Warren County schools as they share end-of-semester presentations.

items.title: Winter Spirit Clinic — Waynesville High School Competition Cheerleaders
items.venue: Waynesville Elementary School gym, 659 Dayton Rd, Waynesville
items.note: The Waynesville High School competition cheerleaders teach a cheer, a chant, a band dance and the fight song. Each participant gets a t-shirt to wear for a halftime performance at the varsity boys basketball game on Friday, Dec. 4. Sign up online with the team's form; tap Details for the flyer.

items.title: Nationwide Emergency Alert System test (TV and radio)
items.note: FEMA and the FCC will test the Emergency Alert System on broadcast and cable TV and radio. It will not go to cellphones. The message will say it is only a test, and no action is needed. If severe weather or a real emergency gets in the way, the backup date is Thursday, Dec. 3.

items.title: All-Village Spartan Send-Off — Regional Final
items.venue: Waynesville High School and along the route, Waynesville
items.note: Waynesville Football invites the whole village to line the route and cheer the Spartans on as they leave for the Division V, Region 20 final against Bishop Fenwick at 7 p.m. at Lakota East High School. The buses turn right out of the school, right on Main Street, then right on State Route 73. Tap Details for the flyer.
